onboardingParity: PairingScreen, ManualConnectionSheet, and PairingConfirmation match iOS PairingView and ManualTokenEntryView/ConnectionSheet 1:1: full-bleed centered Connect to Intent landing (without the top bar or extra footer copy on first-run onboarding), prominent Scan QR Code card with 64dp lime tile and iOS ConnectQR vector, transparent Manual Connection row with aligned 64dp surface tile and iOS ConnectManual vector, 44dp rounded Manual Connection bottom sheet with top-left Close button, uppercase eyebrow labels, three borderless 64dp surface fields (Host / Tailcat Address, Port, API Token with iOS clipboard paste and eye visibility icons), inline validation/probe error, and 64dp Connect button that immediately probes the TLS certificate and opens a single Verify Server Identity (Cancel / Trust & Connect) alert while keeping explicit Fetch certificate gating for untrusted deep links.
workspaceHeaderFade: The workspace list paints a theme-matched soft gradient below the grouping/search controls. It fades in with the initial scroll offset and keeps clipped rows from meeting a hard header edge without changing list padding or hit targets.
workspaceRowTimestamp: Workspace list rows show a compact relative activity timestamp (now, Xm, Xh, Xd, or short date after 7 days, matching iOS Date+Relative and WorkspaceRowView) aligned to the top-right corner of the title row instead of a separate full-date Activity row; workspace details retain the full timestamp.
workspaceDetailParity: Workspace detail matches iOS WorkspaceDetailView across header, Agents, Context, and Changes: removed stale Active/Idle state line and Workspace details button/dialog from the header, styled status summary as muted secondary text beside optional thumbnail, removed static Browser/Terminals/Scripts/New terminal button dump and Current/All filter chips and Search FAB from Agents and Context, updated AgentRow to flat borderless rows on canvas with top-right relative timestamps and no redundant Coordinator banner or Running text row, unified Context Notes and Files into collapsible sections on one scrollable screen without duplicate Spec subtitles, and aligned Changes tree rows flush left with compact branch and divider-separated commit rows.
workspaceTabsAndChangesParity: Workspace content tabs match iOS IntentContentSwitcher: 20dp surface track with 4dp inset, 48dp tabs, and a 16dp foreground pill that slides between tabs with a spring and no ripple. Changes matches iOS WorkspaceChangesView: collapsible uppercase UNSTAGED/STAGED/COMMITS (n) sections with a rotating chevron (shared with Context NOTES/FILES), empty-section text, file tree rows with folder/file icons, 22dp indentation up to depth 5 with 30% guide lines, monospace names, green/red line stats, status labels (Added, Deleted, Untracked, etc.) instead of raw git codes, folder counts and chevrons, and commit rows with author, short hash, and Pushed/Local labels separated by 10% dividers. Android ellipsizes long tree names instead of iOS horizontal scrolling.
launcherTransition: The Intent button morphs between the iOS 80dp circle and 48dp rounded-square close state, with coordinated glyph rotation, shrink and crossfade, a response-0.35/damping-0.85 spring, reversible animation and Android system duration-scale support. Per user direction, its open state uses the shared neutral grey surface and matching foreground, blended with the same animation progress. The modal keeps its anchor through both transitions, fades its scrim/tiles and preserves existing dismissal/action behavior.
iconParity: Android icons are converted 1:1 from the iOS Assets.xcassets SVGs (Close, ChevronLeft/Right/Down, More, Search, Check, Delete, Edit, Settings2, AddIcon, Connection, Night, ClockwiseArrow, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, Paperclip, File, Folder) instead of Material icons. Back buttons use the iOS chevron, overflow menus use the iOS vertical More dots, and every disclosure uses the iOS chevron (rotated when expanded) instead of text glyphs. Terminal arrow keys and suggested-prompt chips use the iOS arrows. Intent launcher tiles use iOS HomeActionTiles icons at 24dp and 30% of the foreground: IntentDandelion for Assistant, AddIcon for New workspace, ConnectionLaptop for Connections, BrightnessRise/BrightnessFull/Night for System/Light/Dark appearance, and Settings2 for Settings.
typographyAndSpacingParity: Typography tokens already match iOS Constants.Typography (Inter 40/28/18/16/14/12, weights 600/550/450, iOS tracking). Screen roles now match iOS: agent previews use bodyS (16), agent and workspace timestamps use subtextXXS (12), workspace row titles use bodyM semibold, root Context notes use bodyM with bodyS children, and workspace group headings use uppercase eyebrow. Spacing follows iOS WorkspaceDetailStyle and WorkspaceList: 64/32 heading padding with 20 between title, repository and summary, 8 above and 48 below the tabs, 36 between agent rows with 24 from avatar to text and 8 between title and preview, 48 between root notes and 24 between children without dividers, 32/12 around workspace group headings, and 20/10 workspace row spacing.
launchSplashParity: While a saved connection connects at launch, Android shows the iOS SplashArtView instead of the Connections list: the LaunchBackground light/dark gradients with the iOS intent_mark_twist_256 then looping intent_mark_pulse_256 Lottie animations at 100dp, tinted to the theme foreground (white in dark), and a static pulse frame when system animations are off. Like iOS .refreshable, the pull-to-refresh spinner appears only for user pulls; the first workspace load shows Loading workspaces… text. The Android 12+ system splash shows the iOS IntentLogo mark on the LaunchBackground top color instead of the app icon on white, the window background uses the LaunchBackground gradient, and a cold start keeps the full-screen splash for at least iOS Constants.Loading.phaseDuration (1.2 s) and until a saved connection connects, then fades out.
contextNoteRowParity: Context note rows match iOS NoteRowView and WorkspaceNoteIcon: 24dp leading icons flush with the page edge act as the disclosure for notes with children (no trailing chevron), titles start 48dp in where child icons begin, children indent 48dp, and there is no status chip. Icons: iOS File for notes, FileList for the spec, a TaskProgressRing for notes with child tasks, rounded 8dp checkboxes (lime fill with check when complete, 30% when cancelled), Eye for review required, and TaskStatusIcon circles for in progress, blocked, discussion needed and waiting, using the iOS TaskStatus colors. The Context Files tree matches iOS WorkspaceFilesView/WorkspaceFileTreeLabel and shares the Changes tree grid: 16dp folder and 13dp file icons from the iOS assets flush with the page edge, 14sp medium monospace names, 36dp rows with 7dp padding, 22dp indentation up to depth 5 with 30% guide lines, no folder chevrons, and loading and empty states indented under their folder.
conversationGridParity: The conversation page follows iOS WorkspaceConversationHeader and the 24dp conversation inset: 48dp back and overflow controls sit on the 24dp page line and end on the same trailing line as the transcript, the title is centered on one line in bodyXSEmphasized (14sp medium) with an Agent subtitle, and the overflow button has no surface circle. Suggested prompts use iOS SuggestedPrompt spacing (20dp label inset, 12dp vertical padding, 56dp minimum height, 20dp radius, 12dp to the arrow), and the composer text starts 20dp in, so prompt labels and the composer placeholder share one inner line. Vertical rhythm follows iOS: 32dp between transcript rows (Conversation.Design.sectionSpacing), 12dp between blocks inside a message (Transcript.toolRowSpacing), one 16dp line under each Markdown paragraph and list (CompactParagraphStyle), 6dp between list items, and suggested prompts 32dp below the message with 8dp between them.
overscrollParity: Scroll containers bounce like iOS instead of using the Android 12 stretch: a drag past the edge moves the content with rubber-band resistance, release springs it back, and a fling that reaches the edge overshoots slightly and settles. Pull-to-refresh still owns the downward pull at the top of refreshable lists.
connectionSwitcherParity: The left connections drawer matches iOS ConnectionSwitcherList: an uppercase CONNECTIONS eyebrow and plain 56dp rows with the iOS ConnectionLaptop icon and the connection name (16sp medium), 16dp padding, 20dp radius and 4dp spacing, centered vertically with 24dp leading and 32dp trailing insets. The active connection uses the iOS selection fill (charcoal in dark mode, white in light mode) instead of an outlined card, and the drawer no longer repeats addresses, status, path or a Manage connections button; those stay on the Connections screen and in Settings.
workspaceSwipeParity: Workspace row swipe actions match iOS WorkspaceSwipeRow: the list runs edge to edge so a swiped row slides to the screen edge, the divider stays on the page inset and fades as the swipe starts, and Archive and Delete are 48dp icon buttons (iOS Archive and Delete icons, Delete in the destructive color) on 20dp rounded surface tiles, 8dp apart, 32dp from the row and aligned to the page trailing line; they scale in with the swipe.
settingsParity: Settings follows iOS SettingsView: uppercase section labels (Connection, New connection, Appearance, Notifications, Support) over 20dp rounded cards of 56dp icon rows with 24dp insets and dividers, using iOS ConnectionLaptop, Connection, Logout, QRCode, Notification, Settings2, DownloadFile and File icons. The current computer shows its path under its name, Disconnect is a destructive row, local notifications use a switch, the diagnostics report and its actions appear inside the Support card, and the version is a single muted footer line. Android keeps Appearance (with a Lock orientation switch, on by default, that holds the phone in portrait) and Android notification settings, which iOS does not have.
workspaceCreationParity: Workspace creation follows iOS CreateWorkspaceView: each step has a 28sp title (Select Project, Select Branch, New Repository, New Workspace) with 48dp heading actions (+ for a new repository, search), uppercase section labels, and the iOS bottom controls (a 48dp Close or Back tile on the left and the lime Next or Create button on the right). Repositories appear in Recent and More sections as 80dp rows with the GitHub icon, name and owner/name; branches appear as rows with an outlined Default badge; the selected row gets the card fill and a green check, and dividers hide around it. The source shows as a labeled card. The agent step follows iOS CreateWorkspaceSpecialistStepView: a Create Workspace title over the CreateWorkspacePrompt card (20dp rounded surface, 24dp padding, multiline editor with the What should we work on? placeholder, attachments and the attach button inside), the CreateWorkspaceSourceCard (folder icon, repository, off branch <branch> or New repository on your connected computer, chevron; tapping goes back), and an uppercase AGENT section of AgentOptionField rows (106dp label beside a 48dp rounded select menu with a chevron) for Specialist (None), Provider, Model (Default) and Reasoning (Auto, disabled with the iOS hint when the model has no levels). The optional title field is removed, as on iOS.
tailcatParity: Tailcat is on by default, matching iOS: release builds bundle the TailcatKit gomobile library built from the intent-hq/ios commit in tailcat/source.ref, and Acknowledgements shows the tailcat BSD 3-Clause notice from iOS AcknowledgementsView when the library is bundled. Direct-only stub builds remain available with -Ptailcat.enabled=false. Acknowledgements is a pushed Settings page like iOS AcknowledgementsView: an uppercase eyebrow per library over a 12dp rounded, 1dp bordered card with the license title, source URL, and selectable muted license text reflowed to the screen width. The Play application ID is dev.intentapp.android, matching the iOS bundle ID dev.intentapp.ios.
scriptsParity: The workspace Scripts screen follows iOS WorkspaceScriptsView, WorkspaceScriptRow and WorkspaceScriptStore: an uppercase SCRIPTS eyebrow over 36dp-spaced rows with the iOS Terminal icon in a 32dp slot 24dp from the text, the name (18sp medium), the command in two lines of monospace, and the iOS status text (Ready, Starting, Running, Restarting, Finished, Failed, Updating, Disconnected) or the run error, with a trailing iOS Play or Globe icon that becomes a spinner while starting. Rows list saved scripts plus scripts found in package.json (using the declared or lockfile package manager), Makefile, Cargo.toml and pyproject.toml, ported from iOS WorkspaceScriptDiscovery; tapping a row saves a manifest script with script.create on first use, starts it unless it is already live, and opens its detected address in the workspace browser once it runs. Swiping a row reveals the iOS StopFill and Delete actions, and a long press or accessibility action offers the same plus Show output. Show output opens a sheet laid out like iOS ScriptMonitorDetailView with the mode, command, exit code, address and script ID, Run or Stop, Open preview, and the latest run's script.output with terminal control codes removed; it refreshes on script events. Loading, empty, error-with-Retry and disconnected states are handled, and script lists follow nextCursor pages. Android adds the output sheet because iOS has no workspace script output view; the protocol has no per-run history, so only the latest run's output is shown.
browsersParity: Browsers follow iOS WorkspaceBrowsersView, NewWorkspaceBrowserView and WorkspaceBrowserView: an uppercase BROWSERS eyebrow over flat rows with the iOS Globe icon in a 32dp tile, an 18sp title, a one-line 14sp address, a Disconnected label when offline and a chevron that fades as the row swipes; swipe left reveals an 88dp red Delete button, long-press offers Delete browser, and TalkBack gets a Delete browser action. Load errors show muted text with Retry. New browser is a sheet with Cancel, an inline title, the lime Open button, an Address field with the localhost:3000 placeholder, and WorkspaceBrowserURL validation; Open creates a browser:<UUID> row and opens it. The browser page has a close header with the page title, the iOS Page unavailable and Reconnect states, and a bottom address bar (back, forward, URL, spinner, reload). Android keeps a standalone Browsers screen with an empty state and + action because it has no workspace-detail resource section; local host names stay as typed because the Android tunnel maps loopback aliases; script.list and browser.listTabs discovery is not merged into the list.
transferParity: Workspace transfer matches iOS WorkspaceTransferSheet with WorkspaceTransferStore/Relay: Transfer workspace / Workspace transferred heading with close; Choose a machine destination menu with a pairing hint when empty; Archive on source machine switch; estimated size and plan warnings; status and error text; Retry when no preview, Transfer workspace, Cancel / Cancel transfer (disabled after commit), and Done. Failed, cancelled and unconfirmed transfers return to the form with iOS copy; finalize failure is a warning on the done screen; relay errors use iOS copy. Android keeps plural warning cleanup and filters destinations by ID and certificate pin (no stored principal).
agentResourcesParity: The workspace Agents tab follows iOS WorkspaceDetailResources: after the agent rows it lists TERMINALS (terminal icon, title, Disconnected when offline; tap opens the terminal and Back returns to Agents; swipe Delete with the iOS Delete terminal? confirmation; long-press Rename or Delete), BROWSERS (saved browsers; tap opens the page) and SCRIPTS (only scripts that have run, iOS hasRun; tap runs, swipe or long-press for stop, delete and output). Headings sit 24dp above their first row and rows are 36dp apart. Resources replace the No agents message, and pull to refresh reloads them. Android differs: a script load error alone does not add the Scripts section, so offline or older desktops do not show a scripts error on the Agents tab.
notes: Android remains under development. The Intent menu close button uses the exact custom Close.svg path and 1.995 stroke from the referenced iOS asset, retaining theme tint and the existing morph animation. The Intent launcher now transitions between the referenced iOS circle/dandelion and rounded-square/close states with reversible spring motion, coordinated size/rotation/scale/crossfade, animated overlay entrance and system animation-scale support. Workspace rows omit description/status-message paragraphs, matching WorkspaceRowView; details retain the full summary. Workspace list corrections use iOS IntentDandelion artwork, left/right edge drawers with accessible heading actions; Android also opens them with a horizontal swipe that starts on the Workspaces heading row, because system Back covers most of the left edge, and Search beside Recent/Repo/Status with grouping preserved. Android retains system Back outside the central gesture exclusion area; archive actions remain in the heading menu. Earlier UI audit fixes reference iOS 1.1.9: Send beside Stop; paged/collapsible questions; compact queues; Tailcat-only manual pairing guidance and pinned trust; reconnect feedback; workspace grouping/search, canonical statuses and repository/PR/activity/attention metadata; detail headings, status images and summaries; inline tasks and relation links; creation source/branch choices and no specialist; transfer review, eligibility and retry; Assistant modal recovery; settings pairing and acknowledgements; workspace-first history; agent groups and watched links; local terminal names and expandable keys; numbered/wrappable text, external PDF readers and searchable Git details; saved browsers and documented script controls. Earlier transport, offline cache, comments, Markdown/Mermaid, attachments, Git, terminals and notifications remain. Preserve explicit TLS trust and Android Back. Not completed: top-level PR browsing, slash skills, note editing, synchronized terminal names, code/diff syntax highlighting, accessible PDF text and remaining iOS features. Native camera/permissions, Tailcat traffic, live reconnect/transfer/script actions, TalkBack/large text, tablet layouts and background notifications still need device checks. Notifications require a connected process and observe the active connection; taps do not switch hosts.
connectionRecoveryParity: The reconnecting state matches iOS ReadOnlyBanner and ConnectionLossPresentation: a floating bottom pill (300dp max, capsule, shadowed surface) with a small spinner and Reconnecting…, which taps open into a 22dp rounded card (360dp max) with Reconnecting to <machine>… · Read-only, the keep-reading guidance, and a Back to Home action. After returning from the background, the pill waits a 1 s grace period so a quick reconnect after unlocking shows nothing. Android has no startup, offline, or certificate states in this pill yet, and uses a fixed 104dp bottom clearance for the Intent launcher instead of iOS's measured chrome clearance.
listSearchParity: List search matches iOS WorkspaceSearchInput in the WorkspaceListView bottom safe-area inset: when search opens, a 56dp rounded (20dp) surface field with a 20dp leading inset and a separate 56dp close button sit at the bottom with 8dp spacing and ride on top of the keyboard, instead of an outlined field under the view switcher. The clear button appears only with text and keeps search open; the close button ends search. Android uses the same input for workspace and file searches.
connectionRecoveryTimingParity: Like iOS ConnectionManager path monitoring and foreground handling, the session recovers without backoff when the activity starts or the default network is gained or lost: a ready session must answer a 5 s system.status probe or it reconnects at once, an attempt started on the old network restarts, and a waiting retry runs immediately. Android probes with an RPC instead of the iOS 15 s heartbeat; OkHttp keeps its 30 s ping.
codeBlockParity: Fenced code blocks match iOS CodeBlockView: an 8dp rounded card with a header row (monospace language label and a Copy action using the iOS Copy and Check icons, showing Copied for 2 s) above horizontally scrolling, unwrapped monospace code with 12dp insets. Unknown fences such as ws-block:cli render as plain code, as on iOS.
scriptWatchPillParity: Script watches match iOS ScriptWatchPills and WorkspaceStatusPill: one 32dp capsule per watch with the iOS Eye icon (16dp), 12dp icon spacing, 16/12dp insets and a single Watching <script> line. The expiry is the accessibility state instead of visible text, and the elapsed line is removed.
